title: Configured skills.paths are not exposed to LouiseLM agents
description:
## Problem

LouiseLM no longer appears to discover or expose skills from the configured global `skills.paths`. A `louiselm.lua` configuration points at a directory containing 34 skills, but asking the active LouiseLM agent which skills are available reports only one unrelated built-in/session skill. Skill loading previously worked with this configuration.

This suggests the configured skill catalog is being dropped between setup, discovery, chat construction, and agent context/native loading.

## Investigation

- Reproduce through the normal `louiselm.setup()` plus `:Louiselm` chat path, not only by calling `require("louiselm.skills").discover()` directly.
- Determine whether the regression is specific to `skills.policy = "native"`, `"inject"`, or both.
- Compare `:checkhealth louiselm` discovery results with the skills actually made available in the resulting session/chat.
- Preserve and surface discovery errors instead of silently reducing the catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a configured `skills.paths` directory containing multiple valid `SKILL.md` entries, a newly opened LouiseLM chat makes every valid discovered skill available according to the effective skills policy.
2. The normal setup/command integration path is covered by a regression test using multiple skills; coverage must fail if the catalog is omitted or reduced to a single skill.
3. Invalid skill entries do not hide valid siblings, and actionable discovery errors identify rejected paths/metadata.
4. `:checkhealth louiselm` and the session/chat behavior agree on whether configured skills were discovered and are available.
5. Focused tests and the full project quality gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed configured skill discovery end to end: follow SKILL.md symlinks after resolving targets, ignore unconsumed optional YAML metadata while validating required fields, remove the unused lyaml dependency gate, keep valid-sibling counts visible in checkhealth, and cover setup-to-chat injection of multiple skills. The real configured generated tree now reports 34 skills and 0 errors. Verification: focused red-green tests; full MiniTest 150/150; stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; git diff --check passed.

title: Preserve multiline chat prompts entered with Shift+Enter
description:
## Problem

In the Markdown chat buffer, Shift+Enter can insert a continuation line while editing the `> ` prompt. Pressing Enter afterward submits only the tracked first line. The continuation is omitted from the ACP prompt, remains visible below the newly inserted response/prompt area, and the model begins responding to incomplete input.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a louiselm chat session and type the first line in the `> ` prompt.
2. Press Shift+Enter to create a new line inside the Markdown quote block.
3. Type a second line.
4. Press Enter to submit.

## Observed

Only the first line is sent to the session. The second line remains stranded at the bottom of the chat buffer while the model responds.

## Expected

The submitted prompt contains every line in the editable prompt block, in order, with intentional newlines preserved. After a successful submit, no submitted continuation line remains as an orphaned draft.

## Code evidence

`Chat:submit()` reads only `view.prompt_line` via `nvim_buf_get_lines(..., view.prompt_line, view.prompt_line + 1, ...)`. `submit_prompt()` then inserts the response separator and next prompt immediately after that one line, so any continuation lines are shifted below the new chat area rather than consumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A two-line prompt entered with Shift+Enter is sent as one prompt containing both lines and their newline.
- All submitted prompt lines are rendered as transcript history and removed from the editable prompt region.
- The next `> ` prompt appears after the response area; no continuation text is left below it.
- Single-line submission and queued-prompt behavior remain unchanged.
- Headless UI tests cover multiline submission through the buffer-facing behavior, including the sent payload and resulting buffer layout.
close_reason: Fixed multiline chat prompt submission by reading and rendering the full prompt block. Added a headless regression test covering payload and buffer layout. Verification: focused chat suite 35/35, full mini.test suite 127/127, stylua --check passed, lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics, git diff --check passed.

title: Invoke native skills through advertised ACP commands
description:
## Goal

Make the local skill picker invoke adapter-native skills exactly once through current ACP command advertisement.

## Scope

- In scope: handle `available_commands_update` per session; every valid update replaces the cache, an empty update clears it, malformed entries are skipped and diagnosed, and duplicate entries remain visible to ambiguity detection.
- In scope: correlate only locally discovered configured skills. Prefer exact `$<skill-name>`; otherwise allow exact `<skill-name>` only when the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description or OpenAI short description.
- In scope: make `$name` win over a colliding built-in `name`; reject ambiguous matches.
- In scope: keep picker selections pending when no command update exists, without guesses or timeouts; re-resolve against the latest cache at actual submission and queued-prompt release.
- In scope: if a command disappears or becomes ambiguous, send nothing and preserve the user's prompt and skill chip with an actionable error.
- In scope: send the advertised command and task as one first text block, such as `/$grill-me stress-test this` for Codex or `/grill-me stress-test this` for Claude.
- In scope: send no LouiseLM catalog or skill body in native mode and leave user-authored slash commands untouched.
- Out of scope: a general ACP command browser, adapter-name heuristics, and injected discovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Command state always reflects the latest valid update and recovers on later updates.
2. Malformed entries do not preserve a stale previous command list.
3. Codex-style dollar commands and Claude-style exact commands resolve using the strict agreed rules.
4. A built-in `plan` cannot steal a local `plan` skill when `$plan` is advertised.
5. Duplicate or weak description-only matches never trigger a command.
6. Picker activation before advertisement waits safely and is late-bound at submission.
7. Disappearing/ambiguous commands preserve unsent user input.
8. Mock ACP tests cover replacement, empty/malformed updates, duplicates, collisions, pending selection, queued release, command formatting, manual slash passthrough, and no-double-send behavior.

## Testing

Drive session command updates and captured prompt blocks through the mock ACP agent. Installed Codex/Claude adapters are manual smoke tests, not authenticated CI dependencies.

title: Resolve static per-agent skill policies and migrate configuration
description:
## Goal

Make `native`, `inject`, and `off` explicit, session-static Agent Skills policies with a native default and no inferred fallback.

## Scope

- In scope: keep skill paths global; add global `skills.policy = "native"` and permit only a per-agent `skills.policy` override.
- In scope: validate policy values through the existing configuration schema and expose the effective policy to session setup, UI status, help, and health.
- In scope: snapshot policy at session creation; never infer it from adapter names, command advertisement, filesystem capabilities, or runtime failures.
- In scope: remove `full_content` with a targeted migration error and remove the dormant `native_supported` automatic-fallback API.
- In scope: `off` disables the local picker and all LouiseLM skill automation; `native` does not require `lyaml` to start but local picker/validation is unavailable without it; `inject` is blocked without it.
- In scope: preserve user-authored slash commands in every policy.
- Out of scope: catalog formatting, native command correlation, runtime profile switching, and per-agent path overrides.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An agent with no override uses `native`.
2. DeepSeek/GLM-style agents can opt into `inject` without affecting Codex/Claude sessions.
3. Unknown policy values and per-agent path overrides fail validation clearly.
4. Legacy `full_content` configuration fails with exact replacement guidance.
5. No runtime event changes an existing session's policy.
6. Missing `lyaml` has the agreed profile-specific effects.
7. UI status can show a simple `skills: on` state while technical policy remains available in help/health.
8. MiniTest covers defaults, overrides, invalid/legacy keys, session snapshotting, dependency gating, off behavior, and lack of fallback.

## Testing

Exercise the declarative schema and session-facing policy API. Do not add adapter-name heuristics to tests or production code.
close_reason: Implemented static native/inject/off per-agent skill policies, lyaml gating, UI/health visibility, migration errors, docs, and deterministic MiniTest coverage; all 147 tests, StyLua, and lua-language-server pass

title: Render submitted prompt contexts as native Neovim folds
description:
## Goal

Keep pre-send chat uncluttered while making every LouiseLM-attached prompt context exactly inspectable after submission.

## Scope

- In scope: before submission, represent manually selected skills and other contexts as compact chips; never display the automatic injected catalog as editable text or a marker.
- In scope: after an accepted prompt, render one closed native Neovim fold for that user turn containing every attached context in exact transport order and exact sent content.
- In scope: include concise context labels in the fold summary and preserve the ordinary visible user prompt.
- In scope: use normal Neovim fold commands and the existing chat buffer/context model; the fold is transcript representation only and must never be resent.
- In scope: retain chips and editable prompt on local send failure or blocked skill read.
- In scope: limit behavior to the live nofile, swap-disabled chat buffer; do not reconstruct folds after session load or Neovim restart.
- Out of scope: tool-call folding, transcript persistence, summary-only context storage, custom fold widgets, and a generic fold framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A pending automatic catalog produces no visible `[context: skill-index]` line.
2. One submitted turn with several contexts produces one closed fold with exact ordered contents.
3. Opening the fold reveals what ACP received, not a lossy summary.
4. The visible user prompt remains distinct from its attached context.
5. Failed local submissions keep pre-send chips and do not create a misleading submitted fold.
6. Reopening or closing folds cannot affect future prompt payloads.
7. MiniTest/headless UI tests cover fold boundaries, summary labels, exact contents/order, failure retention, and no resend.

## Testing

Use native fold APIs in a headless chat buffer and assert both buffer lines/fold ranges and captured ACP payloads.

## Notes

The current buffer is intentionally ephemeral and memory-resident. Documentation must explain that inspectability lasts only for the live chat.

title: Concurrent ACP permission requests deadlock the session
description:
Two parallel tool calls in one agent turn produce two overlapping session/request_permission requests. louiselm opens one vim.ui.select picker per request with no serialization, so the second picker steals the first, the first is answered with outcome=cancelled without user input, and the second is never answered at all. The agent then blocks forever waiting on the permission response, and the session is unrecoverably stuck at status=prompting.

## Observed (session claude/25e0dc43-f1d6-4110-be74-e23b1d9920b7, 2026-08-16 19:45 UTC)

Agent JSON-RPC log ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260816-214042-74168-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:

- id=0  session/request_permission  find / -iname "*bc036951*"   -> answered (Always Allow), tool completed
- id=1  session/request_permission  wc -l ...gardening/....jsonl -> answered outcome=cancelled  (user did NOT choose this)
- id=2  session/request_permission  grep -n -i grill ...         -> NEVER answered

id=1 and id=2 were emitted back to back (19:45:12.63). Transcript
~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/25e0dc43-....jsonl records
"Tool permission request failed: Error: Tool use aborted" for toolu_01NgmPSjG8GXeMfmjuKrvfZZ (wc) 18ms after the grep tool_use, and has no tool_result at all for toolu_01K4jqsnByKAkCN5pJMRhRgU (grep).

Agent pid 74168 was still alive and blocked on id=2 more than 13 minutes later. The grep tool_call stayed "pending" forever; session/prompt never returned.

Proof the user never confirmed either choice: ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/permissions.json holds an always-rule for the find command only (mtime 19:45:04). Had the user actually confirmed "Always Allow" on the wc or grep picker, permission/store would have persisted a rule for it. It did not - the picker was dismissed programmatically, which is exactly what the user reported seeing ("a select picker that was pressed automatically and not by me").

## Symptoms

- Chat header shows "Model responding" forever; status=prompting.
- Typed input reports "Queued for next turn" and never runs, because Session:prompt requires status=="ready".
- One tool is reported to the model as aborted even though the user never denied it, so the model sees a bogus refusal.

## Root cause

1. lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:56 - every agent request is dispatched independently (nvim.schedule out of the fast event). No queue, no per-session serialization of session/request_permission.
2. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:732 prompt_permission -> lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua:11 calls vim.ui.select directly for each request. With an async provider (Snacks picker, which this setup uses) a second vim.ui.select while one is open tears down the first; its callback fires with nil -> cancel_permission responds outcome=cancelled to the wrong/first request, and the surviving picker never delivers a selection for the second request.
   Nothing tracks outstanding permission requests, so a request whose picker dies is never answered and never times out.
3. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:288 - permission_respond sets status back to "prompting" as soon as ANY single response is sent, regardless of other outstanding permission requests. That is why the UI showed "Model responding" instead of "Waiting for permission" while still blocking on id=2.

## Why tests miss it

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua stubs vim.ui.select with a synchronous callback (e.g. lines 172-188, 330-343), which serializes requests implicitly. Real async pickers do not.

## Fix direction

- Serialize permission prompts per session: queue incoming session/request_permission and open the next picker only after the previous one has been answered.
- Track every outstanding request id; guarantee exactly one response per request (fail-closed with outcome=cancelled on UI teardown/dispose so the agent is never left hanging).
- Keep status=="waiting_permission" while any permission request is still outstanding.
- Never let picker teardown cancel a request the user did not act on - prefer re-prompting or a queued prompt over a silent cancel.

## Acceptance

- Regression test with an async vim.ui.select stub that holds callbacks: two overlapping permission requests must produce two pickers shown one after the other and two responses, neither of them a spontaneous cancel.
- Test that disposing/closing while a permission is pending sends exactly one cancelled response per outstanding request.
- Test that status stays waiting_permission until all outstanding permission requests are answered.

## Recovery note

While stuck there is no documented way out except cancelling the turn; investigate whether Session:cancel actually unblocks an agent that is parked in session/request_permission.
close_reason: Fixed in c639f95. Sessions queue session/request_permission and publish one at a time (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua pump_permissions), status stays waiting_permission until the last outstanding request is answered, and a second response for the same request returns 'permission request was already answered'. Session:cancel now answers every outstanding request with outcome=cancelled, which is the recovery path the bug lacked. Remembered rules moved from arrival to publish time so an always choice covers requests already queued. Chat UI answers cancelled instead of dropping a choice made after view teardown. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua 'publishes overlapping permission requests one at a time', 'cancels every outstanding permission request when the turn is cancelled', 'applies a fresh always choice to permission requests already queued'; tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'cancels a queued permission choice after disposal'. Full suite 194 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. Deviation from the filed acceptance criteria: dispose clears the queue instead of writing cancelled responses, because dispose closes the ACP client and kills the agent process.

title: Permission picker Enter moves selection instead of confirming
description:
## Context

Observed in LouiseLM session codex/01a004ba-1d79-7a52-8d92-cec4cfdf1dc7 while committing. The permission picker displayed option 1 (Allow once) selected by default. Pressing Enter moved the option down in the picker instead of confirming it.

## Expected

Enter confirms the currently selected permission option and sends the ACP permission response.

## Actual

The selection/cursor moves down in the picker window; the permission is not immediately confirmed.

## Triage

LouiseLM delegates permission prompts to vim.ui.select. The current user Snacks config sets picker.sources.select.focus = "list" and enables wrap = true/linebreak = true. The recent permissions commit 757134a4 changed remembered-choice handling and option data, but did not change picker key handling. Likely interaction is in the Snacks select provider or its wrapping/focus configuration; reproduce with a minimal vim.ui.select containing the Codex options, then test with select wrapping disabled.

Relevant code: lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua prompt_permission() calls nvim.ui.select(options, ...).
Relevant docs: README.md explains Snacks select wrapping and recommends wrap = false for the select source when rows are not usable.
close_reason: Closed after reproducing with a very long permission option: Snacks vim.ui.select behaved correctly once picker source wrapping was disabled (wrap = false). The screenshot indicated keypresses had reached the underlying readonly chat buffer (E21), not a LouiseLM choice-handling failure. No LouiseLM bug reproduced.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Screenshot reproduction: Snacks picker shows 4/4 results but only two rows are visible in a very short list window; option 1 is highlighted. The underlying louiselm:// buffer reports E21 after attempting :verbose, which is expected because that buffer is nomodifiable; the command was not run in a command-line context. This points toward picker focus/list-window behavior or visual scrolling, not malformed permission choices.

title: Make reporting a session bug easy with a stable session identifier
description:
## Goal

Make it easy to report a louiselm bug against a specific session by telling the maintainer one stable identifier, instead of manually extracting context from the UI or conversation.

## Investigation

The current implementation has two different identifiers:

- The public session state exposes a local runtime id (`state.id`), which is not the ACP persistence id needed to correlate a resumed conversation.
- The agent-side ACP id is stored privately on the session (`acp_session_id`).
- The resume picker formats the title first and only falls back to the ACP id; the id is therefore not guaranteed to be the first visible item.

A bare ACP id may also be ambiguous when multiple configured agents can use the same id, so the most useful report token is the configured agent name plus the ACP session id (or an equivalent stable single-line representation).

## Proposed fix

Expose a deliberate, read-only report identity for the current session and make it easy to copy/quote:

1. Add a public session inspection field or method for the agent-side ACP session id/report identity, with LuaCATS documentation distinguishing it from the local runtime id.
2. Add a small user-facing command/action such as `:LouiselmSessionId` that reports the current session identifier and copies it to the Neovim clipboard when available; it should work for newly created and resumed sessions and fail clearly when no session is attached.
3. Put the report identifier first in the relevant session picker row, keeping title/workspace metadata available after it. Avoid exposing internal implementation fields directly or logging prompts/transcripts.
4. Document a short bug-report workflow: include the identifier, reproduction steps, and expected/actual behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can obtain one stable identifier for the currently displayed session with one command/action.
- The identifier remains useful after `:LouiselmResume` and identifies the ACP conversation, not merely the transient local session object.
- Agent identity is included when needed to avoid cross-agent ambiguity.
- The picker displays the report identifier as its first item/field.
- No prompt, tool payload, token, or other sensitive session content is copied or logged.
- Headless tests cover current-session, resumed-session, no-session, and picker-format behavior.
- README/help documentation explains how to include the identifier when reporting a bug.

## Follow-up

A separate grill-me session can stress-test whether a command, automatic bug-report template, or a richer session diagnostic bundle is the right UX before implementation expands beyond the minimal identifier workflow.
close_reason: Implemented stable agent-scoped ACP report identifiers. Public session snapshots expose acp_session_id; :LouiselmSessionId copies/reports <agent>/<ACP-id>; resume and attached-session picker rows lead with the report identity; README documents the bug-report workflow. TDD covered new, resumed, no-session, clipboard, and picker behavior. Full 131-case MiniTest suite passes; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server reports zero diagnostics; git diff --check passes; dependency graph has no cycles.

title: Document and diagnose Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Goal

Make Agent Skills configuration understandable and diagnosable for users of both known and unfamiliar ACP adapters.

## Scope

- In scope: update README skills/dogfooding sections, schema-generated help and annotations, migration guidance, and checkhealth.
- In scope: explain the three policies, native default, per-agent override, static sessions, natural-language versus picker activation, explicit-only skills, and the no-double-send contract.
- In scope: explain that Agent Skills specifies skill files, ACP is transport, and native command advertisement or Codex-like fallback behavior are host/adapter mechanisms rather than ACP skill specification features.
- In scope: document the fixed injected catalog behavior and 8,000-byte conservative Codex-inspired budget, including truncation/omission ordering and absolute-path privacy.
- In scope: provide platform-neutral `lyaml`/LibYAML installation guidance with common examples, Lua 5.1 ABI guidance for Neovim, no automatic install, and profile-specific missing-dependency effects.
- In scope: document root precedence, relative-path workspace trust, symlink aliases/escapes, skill-folder trust, `allowed-tools` permission limits, and the absence of automatic project roots or trust database.
- In scope: explain that injected implicit activation requires agent-side file access, picker-attached instruction-only skills may work without it, scripts/references/assets still need agent tools, and ACP does not standardize or let health verify this capability.
- In scope: show effective policy and detailed parser/discovery diagnostics in checkhealth, including shadowed/invalid skills, metadata conflicts, symlink escapes, line warnings, and catalog truncation/omission.
- In scope: document live-only fold contents and nofile/swap-disabled memory implications, plus manual installed Codex and Claude smoke procedures.
- Out of scope: authenticated adapter automation, a general ACP command UI, filesystem serving, and tool-call fold UX.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new user can choose `native`, `inject`, or `off` for an unfamiliar adapter from documentation alone.
2. Codex and Claude examples use native mode without duplicate injection; custom DeepSeek/GLM adapter examples show explicit inject overrides.
3. Old `full_content` users receive a direct migration explanation.
4. Checkhealth identifies actionable dependency, path, metadata, shadowing, and budget issues without claiming it can verify agent-side filesystem access.
5. Documentation explicitly labels the Codex-inspired budget/fallback as non-standard and leaves a future-spec reconsideration note.
6. Generated help/annotations and README configuration examples agree.
7. Manual smoke instructions verify native invocation with installed Codex and Claude adapters and injected behavior with a mock/custom adapter.

## Testing

Run documentation/schema consistency checks and health tests. Perform documented manual adapter smoke checks when credentials and installed adapters are available; do not make them CI requirements.

title: Permission picker treats Allow Once as Deny
description:
## Summary

After the fail-closed permission ordering fix, a user who selects the displayed second option, Allow Once, can still send the first option, Deny. Generic vim.ui.select providers may render numbered rows without interpreting a typed number as row selection.

## Reproduction

Session: claude/d0cb6393-4548-4533-937f-614160f5a2b5

1. Ask Claude to perform an operation requiring permission.
2. Deny the first request.
3. Ask Claude to retry and select displayed option 2, Allow Once.
4. Observe Claude receives User refused permission again.

The ACP trace advertised Deny as option 1 and Allow Once as option 2 on both requests.

## Expected

A deliberate Allow Once choice sends its exact ACP optionId. Rejecting, allowing, and cancelling must all be unambiguous regardless of the installed vim.ui provider.

## Actual

Typing the displayed option number can confirm the provider current row instead, so option 2 is interpreted as option 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The permission choice flow does not depend on provider-specific numbered-row key behavior.
2. Choosing Deny sends the deny optionId, and choosing Allow Once sends the allow optionId.
3. Invalid or dismissed choices cancel rather than approve.
4. Agent option labels and identifiers remain distinct and unmodified.
5. Scheduled UI handling and late-choice-after-disposal safety remain covered by headless tests.
close_reason: Replaced provider-dependent permission selection with explicit numbered input, preserving exact ACP option IDs. Added regression coverage for Claude's Deny/Allow Once options, invalid and dismissed input, distinct labels, scheduling, and disposal. Verification: 43 focused UI tests and 184 full MiniTest cases pass; installed Snacks input smoke returns typed 2; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Investigate diff edit approval UX
description:
## Context

After asking LouiseLM to create a file, the plugin opened a `louiselm-diff` buffer. The latest screenshot (`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0457_1920x1200_1786244259.png`) shows the target path, `--- original`, `+++ proposed`, and an otherwise empty buffer. No visible accept/reject/close actions or instructions are presented, and Neovim is in insert mode.

## Investigation

Determine the intended lifecycle for an agent-proposed file edit and whether this diff view is currently incomplete, incorrectly rendered, or intentionally only a review surface. Trace the permission/edit/diff flow and document how a user should:

- understand what changed;
- accept/apply the proposed edit;
- reject it;
- cancel or return to the conversation;
- handle an empty/new-file diff;
- recover if the diff buffer is closed or the proposed edit becomes stale.

Assess the UX from a first-time user perspective, including discoverability of keymaps/commands, mode choice, statusline/help text, and whether approval belongs in the diff view, a permission prompt, or both.

## Exit criteria

- Reproduce the flow with a deterministic test or documented local scenario.
- Identify the root cause of the empty/unactionable presentation, if it is a bug.
- State the intended user-facing contract and recommended minimal UX changes.
- Add implementation follow-up beads tasks if the investigation finds separate fixes.
- Add or update headless UI behavior coverage for the confirmed contract where practical.
close_reason: Added discoverable diff approval instructions and normal-mode focus; verified full test and quality gates.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Investigation complete. The diff controller already had buffer-local normal-mode mappings: a accepts, d/q reject. The screenshot was unfriendly because the review buffer provided no instructions and inherited insert mode from the chat prompt, making those mappings undiscoverable/unusable. The diff is a permission review; accept sends the ACP allow response and the agent performs the write. Added an explicit instruction line and return to normal mode on focus. Existing behavior tests plus the new render assertion pass; no separate apply bug was reproduced.

title: Restored chat crashes while rendering replayed history
description:
## Problem

Loading an existing ACP/Codex session works, but the chat UI crashes when replayed assistant history arrives. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:690` performs arithmetic on `view.transcript_tail`, which is nil for a newly attached restored session.

## Reproduction

1. Create a session with Codex ACP and exit Neovim.
2. Load the ACP session with `sessions:load_session(...)`.
3. Attach it to `Chat`.
4. Observe `vim.schedule callback ... chat/init.lua:690: attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Restored assistant history renders without an error.
- New-session streaming behavior remains unchanged.
- Add a focused regression test covering a replayed chunk on an attached restored session.
close_reason: Fixed restored assistant chunk rendering fallback and added regression coverage. Focused chat tests: 30 passed; full mini.test suite: 115 passed; stylua --check and lua-language-server diagnostics passed.

description: Reproduction A: from the repository root run nvim -u tests/minimal_init.lua, then execute :LouiselmChat (the reported spelling was :LouisLMChat). The chat buffer opens as '# default · session-1' but shows 'Error: ACP session/new failed: Invalid params' and an empty prompt. Expected: the documented minimal init provides a working out-of-the-box chat session with the default agent, or reports a specific actionable setup error. Reproduction B: run nvim -u manual_init.lua, update packages, then execute :LouiselmChat (the reported spelling also included :LuiseLmChat). title: ACP session options and resource telemetry UX
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM can select an adapter only when the first chat is created, and it currently discards ACP session configuration options and usage/context updates. Users cannot change an agent-advertised model or reasoning setting after startup, cannot see which settings are active, and cannot tell whether a long autonomous session is approaching its context limit or waiting on a permission request. Starting multiple sessions also lacks explicit navigation and cleanup controls.

## Solution

Add a generic ACP session-controls and observability UX. After `session/new` becomes ready, open a token-free setup overview of all supported agent-advertised select and boolean options; allow idle-only changes through a public chat method and `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, refreshing the complete option list after each update. Add explicit `:LouiselmCancel`, `:LouiselmNewSession`, `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, and `:LouiselmCloseSession` commands. Keep existing sessions running when a new one starts, expose their state through compact headers and switcher rows, and dispose sessions explicitly when closed. Render passive context-pressure states, reported cumulative cost, active settings, lifecycle state, permission waiting, compaction/tool activity, and optional experimental per-turn usage fields without estimating tokens or prices.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to choose model and other ACP session options before my first prompt, so that each new session starts with deliberate settings.
2. As a user, I want to change supported options while a session is idle, so that future turns use the new configuration without restarting the session.
3. As a user, I want busy sessions to refuse option changes and offer explicit cancellation, so that autonomous turns are not reconfigured mid-flight.
4. As a user, I want to see active settings, lifecycle state, context pressure, cost, and reported usage, so that I can monitor long-running work.
5. As a user, I want to create, switch between, and close concurrent sessions, so that multiple adapters can work without leaking processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A ready new session with supported ACP config options opens an overview picker before the first prompt; Esc accepts agent defaults and an agent with no supported options skips the picker.
2. The overview renders every supported select/boolean option in agent order, supports selecting values, applies `session/set_config_option`, replaces the local list with the complete response, and handles agent-pushed `config_option_update` notifications.
3. Option changes are rejected while prompting, cancelling, or waiting for permission; `:LouiselmCancel` requests cancellation and late callbacks cannot revive disposed UI or sessions.
4. The client advertises boolean config-option support and ignores unknown future option types while rejecting malformed consumed fields.
5. `:LouiselmNewSession` chooses an adapter, creates a separate session, and opens its setup picker without cancelling existing sessions; `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects attached sessions using compact agent/state/options/context/cost rows.
6. `:LouiselmCloseSession` confirms only for active or permission-blocked sessions, disposes the selected session/process, removes its chat buffer, and leaves other sessions running.
7. Session headers show exact lifecycle/activity state, all active options, context used/size/percentage with passive 75/90/95% warning states, stale context after model changes until refreshed, and reported cumulative cost when available.
8. Completed turns append a compact usage footer only for reported fields; optional experimental usage fields are validated defensively, never estimated or supplemented with adapter-specific fallbacks.
9. Compaction remains agent-owned: render generic ACP tool/compaction activity and context-meter changes, but add no LouiseLM manual compaction API in this phase.
10. Headless session snapshots/events expose typed configuration, lifecycle, permission, context, cost, and usage state for a future monitor; no swarm dashboard or orchestration is included.

## Implementation Notes

- Extend the session lifecycle and ACP validation at the shared boundary; preserve complete option-list replacement and asynchronous main-loop scheduling.
- Enrich `session:inspect()` and typed events rather than deriving telemetry from rendered buffers.
- Keep `LLM_MODEL` in the caller-owned schema/config example; do not add a universal built-in schema that rejects provider-specific environment variables.
- Preserve agent-provided defaults, session history, cumulative cost, and existing slash-command passthrough. Mark context telemetry stale after model changes until the agent reports a new effective window.

## Testing Notes

- Add focused mini.test coverage for option parsing, dependent option refresh, boolean capability advertisement, malformed/unknown options, idle-only transitions, cancellation, permission waiting, and disposal/late results.
- Add headless UI smoke tests for setup/overview flow, command behavior, headers, passive thresholds, usage footer omission, compaction/tool rendering, multiple-session navigation, and close confirmation.
- Exercise ACP notifications and process callbacks through scheduled production boundaries; use the mock ACP agent and no real credentials or agent binaries.

## Out of Scope

- Manual compaction or a hard-coded `:LouiselmCompact` command.
- A generic advertised-command picker.
- A swarm dashboard, orchestration, capacity policy, worktree isolation, or subagent aggregation.
- Adapter-specific usage parsers, pricing tables, tokenizers, or cache-cost estimates.
- A universal built-in configuration schema.
close_reason: Implemented ACP select/boolean session options, typed lifecycle/context/cost/usage state, setup and multi-session commands, safe scheduled UI updates, documentation, and passing StyLua/LuaLS/95-test gates

title: Rejected commit approval can be bypassed by retrying the request
description:
## Summary

A user rejection of a privileged Git commit did not persist as a denial. After the user repeated the same `commit and sync` request, the agent retried the rejected operation and successfully committed and pushed changes.

## Reproduction

Session: `01a00708-4889-7501-a873-52601d5333fd`

1. In `/home/lotso/dotfiles`, ask the agent to `commit and sync` with uncommitted changes.
2. When approval is requested for the Git metadata write, reject it.
3. Repeat `commit and sync`.
4. Observe that the agent retries `git add ... && git commit ...`, then runs `git pull --rebase origin main` and `git push origin main` successfully.

Observed commit: `deb5744 chore(beads): update WAL certificates`.

## Expected

A rejected approval must remain denied for that action/request. The agent should report that the operation was not authorized and must not retry the rejected privileged command or perform the subsequent push unless the user explicitly grants a fresh approval through the approval control. Repeating the natural-language request alone must not bypass the rejection.

## Actual

The next turn treated the earlier rejection as a temporary environment blocker and retried the same privileged operation. The retry succeeded and the changes were committed and synced.

## Impact

Users can lose control over repository mutations after explicitly rejecting an approval prompt. This is an authorization and safety issue affecting commit/push workflows.

## Evidence

The session log records the first tool result as `Rejected("rejected by user")`, followed by a second `commit and sync` turn whose tool calls performed commit, pull/rebase, and push.
close_reason: Fixed permission picker to place typed rejection choices before approvals, preventing numbered-picker fallback from selecting Allow Once. Regression failed before the fix and passes; all 183 MiniTest cases, StyLua, LuaLS, and git diff --check pass.

title: Resume restores session but reports malformed ACP session/load result
description:
## Summary

`:LuiselmResume` restores the requested session, but reports:

`louiselm: ACP session/load returned a malformed result`

Observed while resuming the session for: https://a16z.com/knowing-when-to-stop-the-art-of-making-a-loop-converge/?utm_source=tldrai

## Expected behavior

A successfully restored session should resume without a malformed-result error. If the ACP response is accepted and the session is usable, do not report it as malformed; otherwise fail the resume operation clearly and leave state consistent.

## Actual behavior

The session is put back/restored, while louiselm emits the malformed `ACP session/load` diagnostic.

## Investigation notes

Likely a mismatch between the ACP `session/load` result validation and the subsequent resume state transition, or an error being reported after a usable result has already been applied. Reproduce with `:LuiselmResume` on the session described above and inspect the raw response shape and validation boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Resuming a valid saved session does not emit the malformed-result error.
- Malformed `session/load` responses still fail safely and produce a specific diagnostic.
- Resume state is not partially applied when validation fails.
close_reason: Fixed ACP v1 session/load response validation: accept object responses without requiring sessionId, preserve replayed config options when absent, and reject JSON null. TDD regression failed first on {}; focused session tests pass; full 128-case MiniTest suite passes; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server reports zero diagnostics; git diff --check passes; dependency graph has no cycles.

title: Display the requested command in permission pickers
description:
## Problem

The command permission picker identifies only the operation kind and the available decisions. It does not show the command being approved or denied. In the attached observation, after the user entered `retry`, the picker showed only `Deny`, `Allow Once`, and `Always Allow`; the actual `git add ... && git commit ... && git push` command was visible only in a wrapped `[tool]` transcript line behind the picker.

This is unsafe and confusing UX, especially for persistent approval choices. The user should not have to correlate a possibly obscured or stale tool transcript line with the active permission request.

## Evidence

- Screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260816_0743_950x1123_1786858980.png`
- Observed with the Claude ACP adapter after asking `retry`.
- Codex may expose more command context, so compare Claude- and Codex-shaped permission payloads rather than assuming the limitation is adapter-specific.
- Current code already normalizes `data.operation.command`, but `prompt_permission` builds the prompt from only `operation.kind` and formats each item from only the ACP option label. This suggests that the shared UI drops command context that is already available.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a chat using the Claude ACP adapter.
2. Trigger a command requiring permission; denying or failing it and then entering `retry` reproduces the observed sequence.
3. Wait for the command permission picker.
4. Observe that the picker shows approval choices but not the command governed by them.

## Expected

The active permission UI clearly identifies the exact command being approved or denied, including for long or compound shell commands. The complete command must remain inspectable without dismissing the picker or inferring it from the background transcript.

## Actual

The picker prompt is only `louiselm permission (command):`; its entries contain only decision labels.

## Scope

- Surface command context from the normalized permission operation at the decision point.
- Preserve literal command content; do not reconstruct a potentially misleading shell command from lossy data.
- Verify behavior with Claude- and Codex-shaped ACP requests and avoid depending on adapter-specific option labels.
- Keep file-edit diff review and unrelated tool-call rendering unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every command permission request with a valid normalized command shows that exact command in the active permission UI before a response can be selected.
2. Long, wrapped, and compound commands remain fully inspectable without relying on transcript lines or tool-call IDs.
3. ACP option names and identifiers remain exact, rejection choices remain first, picker dismissal still cancels, and responses still return the selected option ID.
4. Malformed or unknown operations use an explicit safe fallback and never claim to display a command that was not received.
5. Headless UI tests cover Claude- and Codex-shaped command requests, a long compound command, the safe fallback, scheduling, and the existing fail-closed selection behavior.
close_reason: Displayed exact normalized command JSON in the active permission picker prompt with an explicit unavailable-details fallback. Added Claude/Codex/unknown UI regression coverage and documented behavior. Verification: focused chat suite 48/48; full MiniTest suite 189/189; stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; git diff --check passed.

title: Permission pickers from two sessions can still collide
description:
The permission queue added in c639f95 (louiselm-4wx) is per session. vim.ui.select is a process-wide resource: two attached chat sessions that each reach a permission request at the same time still open two pickers, and an async provider such as the Snacks picker tears the first one down. That reproduces the louiselm-4wx failure across sessions - one request answered cancelled without the user acting, the other left unanswered and blocking its agent.

Not fixed with louiselm-4wx because the narrowest boundary for the reported single-session deadlock was the session, and a process-wide picker queue means module-level mutable state, which AGENTS.md section 7 warns against.

Repro sketch: attach two sessions, prompt both so each hits an ask-human permission in the same window, and observe both pickers.

Options to weigh:
- Serialize decision UI in louiselm.ui.chat across views (the chat controller already owns every view and the diff review, so it has a clear owner and lifecycle for the queue).
- Or serialize in louiselm.ui.picker, which also covers the session, skill, and agent pickers, but introduces a module singleton.

Whatever the layer, the invariant is the same as louiselm-4wx: at most one decision UI open at a time, and every ACP permission request answered exactly once.
close_reason: Fixed in 0ed18d0. Chose the chat controller over louiselm.ui.picker: it already owns every view and the diff review, so the queue has a clear owner and lifecycle instead of a module singleton (AGENTS.md section 7), and it covers reviews as well as pickers. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua now queues decisions across all views (queue_decision/pump_decisions/open_decision), releases the slot exactly once per decision, and cancels what it cannot host: chat disposal, an event delivered to a torn-down view, and a select provider that throws. lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua adds a BufWipeout handler because review buffers are bufhidden=wipe - navigating away used to abandon the request unanswered, which would have stalled the queue. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'opens one permission decision at a time across sessions', 'cancels permission decisions still queued when the chat is disposed', 'cancels a permission request delivered after disposal'; tests/ui/diff_spec.lua 'cancels the permission request when its review buffer is wiped'. chat_spec now restores vim.schedule/vim.ui.select in post_case, because a failing expectation skipped a test's own restore and broke MiniTest itself. Full suite 196 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. Not covered: pickers louiselm opens for its own commands (session options, skills, agents) are still unqueued and can collide with a permission decision.

title: Design persistent ACP permission UX
description:
## Goal

Decide and implement how louiselm should remember ACP permission choices such as Allow for Session and Allow Commands Starting With a command prefix.

## Current state

The chat UI displays permission options supplied by the ACP adapter and forwards the selected optionId. louiselm does not persist those choices itself. ACP defines allow_always as remembering the choice but does not prescribe the storage mechanism.

## Scope

- Grill and document the desired UX and trust model for once, session, workspace, command-prefix, and permanent approvals.
- Decide whether louiselm, the ACP adapter, or both own persistence and enforcement.
- Define storage location, scope/keying, revocation/editing UX, and behavior across sessions, adapters, workspaces, and restarts.
- Implement the agreed behavior with tests and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Permission choices have clear, truthful lifetime/scope semantics.
- Persisted rules cannot silently broaden command or file scopes.
- Users can inspect and revoke remembered rules.
- Behavior is covered by deterministic tests and documented for headless and chat consumers.

## Out of scope

- Changing ACP protocol semantics or adding adapter-specific compatibility shims before the UX decision.
close_reason: Implemented exact workspace-and-adapter permission memory, atomic persistent state, option-kind replay, headless list/revoke APIs, file lifetime selection, and :LouiselmPermissions

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Agreed UX direction from grill session:

- louiselm owns remembered permission decisions; no user-configurable rule object initially.
- Default scope is current workspace + current ACP adapter.
- Command rules match exact argv prefixes; no shell strings, regexes, or substring matching.
- Persist state in a user-level file under Neovim stdpath("state"), never the project repo.
- Add :LouiseLmPermissions to inspect and revoke remembered rules.
- allow_once/reject_once are not saved; allow_session is memory-only for the ACP session; allow_always/reject_always are persisted.
- Commands and file edits have separate rule types.
- If a later adapter request lacks a compatible option kind, fail closed and ask the user again; never infer from labels.

title: Send bounded hidden skill catalogs in inject mode
description:
## Goal

Provide natural-language skill discovery to injected agents without visible context markers, unbounded prompts, or duplicate delivery.

## Scope

- In scope: serialize implicit skills using the Agent Skills `<available_skills><skill>...` XML shape with escaped name, description, and absolute configured-alias location.
- In scope: prepend the fixed agreed behavioral instructions and cap the complete serialized hidden block at 8,000 UTF-8 bytes, including preamble and wrappers.
- In scope: preserve the preamble and all possible names/paths, shorten descriptions fairly and codepoint-safely first, then omit the deterministic name/path-sorted tail if minimum metadata still cannot fit.
- In scope: exclude explicit-only skills from the model catalog while retaining them in the picker; expose omitted/truncated diagnostics.
- In scope: build the catalog only for a new session, hold it locally, and attach it as a separate hidden first text block to the first accepted non-slash model prompt.
- In scope: defer catalog and ordinary attached contexts across user-authored slash prompts; consume the catalog when prompt submission returns a valid ACP request id. Do not resend after accepted cancellation, crash, or uncertain failure.
- In scope: explicit picker activation attaches the exact complete SKILL.md once for that activation; a selected-file read failure blocks submission and preserves the prompt/selection.
- Out of scope: resumed-session reinjection, synthetic catalog turns, recursive resource embedding, native command invocation, and transcript persistence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No `[context: skill-index]` or catalog text is rendered before submission.
2. The entire hidden block never exceeds 8,000 bytes and is validly truncated at UTF-8 boundaries.
3. Natural-language prompts receive one catalog per new injected session; explicit-only skills never appear in it.
4. Slash commands defer rather than consume attached skill context.
5. Synchronous local failure retains the catalog, while any accepted request consumes it exactly once.
6. A deliberate re-selection may attach the same skill on a later turn, but one activation never sends it twice.
7. Resumed or external sessions do not receive a guessed catalog; documentation directs users to start a new session when provenance is uncertain.
8. MiniTest and mock ACP coverage assert block ordering, budgeting, XML escaping, slash deferral, request-id consumption, failure/cancel behavior, picker reads, and no-double-send invariants.

## Testing

Use byte-counting and multibyte fixtures for the budget. Assert exact ACP prompt block arrays through the mock agent.

## Notes

The 8,000-byte rule is a conservative adaptation of Codex fallback behavior, not an ACP or Agent Skills specification requirement.

title: louiselm.nvim: pure ACP client for Neovim — v1 core + phased roadmap
description:
## Problem Statement

As a daily Neovim + agent user, my current plugin (codecompanion.nvim) fights my workflow in three ways. First, config mistakes fail silently: a mistyped key is absorbed by deep-merge and the feature it configures is skipped without a word. Second, its architecture is a general adapter abstraction normalizing HTTP providers and ACP into one interface, while I use exclusively ACP agents (claude-agent-acp, codex-acp, acp-llm-adapter, copilot ACP) — I pay the complexity of a layer I do not use. Third, it gives me no path to the feature I actually want next: a swarm of agents collaboratively working a queue of beads tasks. My core workflow — grill an idea in chat, converge on a plan, convert the plan into beads via skills — must keep working, uniformly, across all my agents.

## Solution

louiselm.nvim: a pure ACP client for Neovim. Agents are external processes declared in config; anything non-ACP reaches the plugin through external bridges (acp-llm-adapter, opencode acp), never through in-plugin providers. The core is built swarm-ready from day one: a multi-session registry with a headless Lua API, typed events, pluggable permission policies, and addressable sessions — so the future orchestrator is an additional consumer of the public API, not a rewrite. Configuration is validated militantly against a single declarative schema that also generates the LuaCATS types and the documentation. Skills use an explicit per-agent native/inject/off policy: native delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter, inject uses a hidden bounded local catalog, and off disables LouiseLM skill automation.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to declare each agent (command, args, env, options) in my config, so that adding a backend is a config entry, never plugin code.
2. As a user, I want any unknown config key to produce a hard error with a fuzzy "did you mean" suggestion, so that typos can never silently disable a feature.
3. As a user, I want wrong types or invalid values to error with the expected type, the received value, and a valid example, so that I can fix mistakes without reading source.
4. As a user, I want all config errors collected and reported in one structured report, so that I fix everything in a single pass instead of a fix-reload loop.
5. As a user, I want the plugin to refuse to start on invalid config, so that I am never unknowingly running on silently substituted defaults.
6. As a user, I want deprecated keys to warn with a migration path, so that upgrades guide me instead of breaking me.
7. As a user, I want editor completion and type checking while writing my config, so that most mistakes are caught before the validator ever runs.
8. As a user, I want :checkhealth to re-run validation plus environment checks (agent binaries on PATH, versions, skill paths exist), so that a broken setup is diagnosable in one command.
9. As a user, I want a chat buffer with streamed markdown and a visible tool-call timeline, so that I can follow what the agent is doing while it does it.
10. As a user, I want to pick which agent a new session uses and switch between concurrent sessions, so that several conversations can live side by side.
11. As a user, I want agent-requested file edits and commands gated by a permission flow, so that nothing touches my system without policy saying so.
12. As a user, I want agent file edits reviewable as diffs, so that I can inspect changes before or after approving them.
13. As a user, I want permissions evaluated by pluggable policy objects with "ask the human" merely the default, so that future autonomous sessions can run scoped auto-approval policies without core changes.
14. As a user, I want to mention the current buffer, send a visual selection, and fuzzy-pick files into the conversation, so that pointing the agent at context is one gesture.
15. As a user, I want slash commands advertised by the agent over ACP to appear in the chat's command menu, so that agent capabilities surface without client-side duplication.
16. As a user, I want my central Agent Skills / SKILL.md repo available to injected agents and the local picker, while native adapters retain ownership of their own discovery, so that one skill tree works without duplicate delivery.
17. As a user, I want an explicit per-agent skills policy (native, inject, off), defaulting to native with no runtime inference or fallback, so that each adapter has one understandable skill owner.
18. As a user, I want ordered, deterministic, symlink-aware local discovery with duplicate and escape diagnostics, so that injected and picker-visible skills resolve predictably.
19. As a user, I want a skill invocation picker that sends one advertised command in native mode or one complete SKILL.md in inject mode, so that explicit activation is predictable and never duplicated.
20. As a user, I want my grill-me → plan → beads workflow to run purely through skills and the agent executing the beads CLI itself, so that the plugin core stays tracker-ignorant.
21. As a plugin consumer (or future orchestrator), I want a headless Lua API — create session against a named agent, prompt, receive streamed updates via callbacks, cancel, dispose — so that everything the UI does is scriptable without UI.
22. As a plugin consumer, I want typed events emitted for every session lifecycle moment (chunk, tool call started/finished, permission requested, turn done, error), so that dashboards and orchestrators can subscribe without patching internals.
23. As a user, I want every session addressable by id with inspectable state (agent, status, working dir, current turn), so that a future swarm dashboard has substrate to read.
24. As a user, I want a crashed or misbehaving agent process to surface as a loud, specific session error — never a hang or a silent death — so that failure modes are as strict as config validation.
25. As a contributor, I want the ACP layer conformance-tested against a mock agent in CI, so that protocol correctness is verified without real LLMs or API keys.

## Implementation Decisions

- Pure ACP client, hard boundary: no in-plugin HTTP providers ever; non-ACP backends go through external bridges. Internally one small agent interface with ACP as its sole implementation, preserving the seam for a hypothetical future transport.
- Five hard architectural constraints checked against every PR: (1) multi-session registry, no singleton chat; (2) headless API with the UI as its first consumer; (3) typed event system; (4) permission policies as pluggable objects, human prompt as default policy; (5) sessions addressable, listable, inspectable.
- Modules: schema (config DSL, validator, error reporter; single source generating LuaCATS types and vimdoc), acp (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio via vim.system pipes, typed against the protocol schema), session (registry, headless API, events, process lifecycle), permission (policy engine), skills (discovery, index injection, per-agent policy, overlap detection), ui.chat, ui.diff, health, and a dev-only mock ACP agent.
- Config validation is militant: unknown key or wrong type is a hard error; errors are collected exhaustively then reported; plugin refuses to start on any error; deprecated keys warn with migration path.
- Skills: Agent Skills defines the file format and ACP remains transport. Global paths feed LouiseLM-managed discovery; global policy defaults to native and an agent may override only native|inject|off. Native sends no catalog/body and resolves picker activation through the adapter's latest advertised commands. Inject sends one hidden, 8,000-byte bounded metadata catalog on a new session and one complete SKILL.md per explicit activation. Off disables automation. Policy is session-static, never inferred, and never falls back at runtime.
- Chat context is deliberately thin: buffer mention, visual selection, file picker, agent slash-command passthrough, skill picker. Agents explore the project themselves; the client points.
- Tech foundation: Neovim floor = latest stable at release, moving forward aggressively; no UI/framework runtime dependencies (no plenary, no nui); `lyaml` plus LibYAML is the explicit conditional runtime dependency for LouiseLM-managed local skill discovery, replacing a custom YAML parser; picker integrations are configured and validated, never silently auto-detected; LuaCATS everywhere with lua-language-server as a CI gate.
- Phasing: P0 foundation (schema, acp, session, agent defs) → P1 daily driver (chat, permissions, diff, context, explicit skill profiles; exit criterion: codecompanion uninstalled, grill-me → beads works on all four agents) → P2 comfort (inline assistant on the same session core, history via ACP session/load, skill-profile ergonomics, multi-session UX) → P3 swarm (opens with its own grill-me).
- Rust is welcome where it earns its place: the swarm orchestrator binary is the named candidate (long-running external process, async runtime, same ecosystem as beads_rust); the core editor-side client stays pure Lua.

## Testing Decisions

- mini.test as the sole, dev-only test dependency.
- schema, acp, session, permission, and skills get full headless unit coverage; the headless API constraint exists partly to make this trivial.
- acp and session additionally get integration coverage driving the mock ACP agent end to end (spawn, initialize, session, prompt, streamed updates, permission round-trip, cancel, agent-crash surfacing).
- A good test here exercises a module through its public interface only; the five architectural constraints are themselves enforced by tests (e.g. two concurrent sessions prompting simultaneously is a required passing case from P0).
- UI modules get smoke tests via child Neovim processes; no pixel-level assertions.
- Validator and skills tests include typo'd keys, wrong types, valid-looking-but-unknown sections, YAML/semantic failures, ordered duplicate precedence, symlink aliases/escapes, native command collisions, injected budget boundaries, and exact no-double-send behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Completion / ghost text: dropped permanently; other plugins own that space.
- In-plugin HTTP or provider adapters of any kind.
- A prompt library separate from skills.
- The swarm orchestrator's design (in-nvim vs external Rust binary, scheduling, worktree isolation): deferred to a dedicated grill-me that opens Phase 3. This epic only guarantees its prerequisites.
- Beads-specific core code; the optional beads dashboard/picker is a future extension on the public API.
- RAG, indexing, web search: agent-side concerns.

## Further Notes

- Ecosystem bet acknowledged: louiselm wagers on ACP's continued adoption (Zed-originated; gemini-cli, opencode, goose, amp, claude, codex all speak it). The internal agent interface is the hedge.
- Risk: ACP spec evolution (e.g. session/load, command advertisement) may shift; the protocol layer should pin a spec version and negotiate capabilities explicitly.
- The user's central skill repo pattern (~/.config/agentskills) is the reference LouiseLM-managed deployment. Discovery preserves configured aliases, canonicalizes for cycles/deduplication, warns on escapes, and treats roots as trusted prompt/plugin-like input.
- Follow-up work items after this epic lands: per-phase decomposition via to-beads-feature / to-beads-tasks, starting with P0.

title: Typing during active turn inserts red buffer error
description:
## Reproduction

## Expected
Typing while it is not the user's turn should be safely rejected, queued, or otherwise handled without a red traceback or corrupted chat buffer. Any user-facing feedback should be intentional and clear.

- Second screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0501_1920x1200_1786244505.png`

- Identify whether the root cause is newline-containing content being passed as one `nvim_buf_set_lines` replacement item, a turn-state race, or both.

title: Queue one next-turn chat prompt while the session is busy
description:
## Problem

Pressing Enter in the chat while the model is responding currently mutates the transcript first, then calls `Session:prompt()`. Because the session is not `ready`, the prompt is rejected and the chat records both a phantom user turn and `Error: session is not ready`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a louiselm chat session and submit a prompt that produces a response long enough to remain active.
2. While the session status is `prompting`, type another message on the chat input line and press Enter.
3. Observe that the input is appended as though it were submitted, followed by `Error: session is not ready`, even though ACP rejected the prompt.

## Expected behavior

The chat owns one pending next-turn prompt per attached session. Pressing Enter during an active turn commits the current input as that session's queued prompt. It remains outside the transcript and sends automatically only after that turn definitively completes or cancellation completes.

## Decisions

- Queue only in `prompting`, `waiting_permission`, and `cancelling`; ordinary ready-state submission remains immediate.
- Support exactly one queued prompt per session, including slash commands.
- Keep queued state with its session when switching chat buffers.
- Show `Queued for next turn` beside the input using virtual text, without modifying prompt text.
- A queued prompt is committed by Enter. Editing it returns it to draft state and requires Enter to recommit, preventing a partial edit from auto-sending.
- Snapshot attached file/selection context when the prompt is committed.
- Release the queue only at a definitive active-turn completion boundary, not on unrelated generic `ready` transitions.
- User cancellation preserves and sends the queued prompt after cancellation completes. A genuine session failure preserves it as a draft and does not send it.
- Append the user message to the transcript only after `Session:prompt()` accepts it.
- If submission fails, preserve the draft and use an editor notification; do not append an `Error:` transcript line for a prompt that was never accepted.
- During `starting` or `configuring`, Enter preserves a draft and notifies instead of queuing. Never queue in `error` or `disposed`.
- Closing a session warns explicitly that its queued prompt will be discarded. Disposal guarantees queued work cannot send later.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Enter during each active-turn state queues one prompt without adding either the prompt or an error to the transcript.
2. On normal turn completion, the committed prompt and its snapshotted context are submitted exactly once and only then appear in transcript history.
3. On completed user cancellation, the committed prompt submits exactly once; on session error it remains an unsent draft.
4. Editing a committed queued prompt makes it a draft and prevents auto-send until Enter recommits it.
5. A second queued turn cannot be accumulated; state is isolated per attached session and survives session switching.
6. Slash commands use the same queue path.
7. Startup/configuration/error/disposed states never create queued work or transcript errors from rejected input.
8. Closing/disposal clears pending work, warns when appropriate, and late scheduled events cannot submit it.
9. Add focused headless chat tests for state transitions, async scheduled event delivery, exactly-once submission, context ownership, switching, failure, cancellation, and disposal. Follow red-green-refactor and run the full required quality gates.

## Scope

- In scope: chat input/queued-prompt state, presentation, lifecycle handling, and behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP to allow concurrent prompts, queuing multiple future turns, or changing session-core readiness rules.
close_reason: Implemented one per-session queued next-turn prompt with virtual-text state, edit invalidation, context snapshots, turn/cancellation release, rejection preservation, close/disposal safety, and README documentation. title: Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently injects one global skill index into every session, including adapters such as Codex and Claude that already provide native Agent Skills support. This exposes an implementation marker in chat, wastes context, can send a skill twice, and leaves users unable to understand which component discovers or invokes a skill.

## Solution

Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles. Global skill paths remain shared, the default policy is `native`, and an agent may override only `skills.policy` with `native`, `inject`, or `off`. Native mode delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter. Inject mode provides a hidden, bounded Agent Skills catalog and attaches a selected full SKILL.md only once per activation. Off disables LouiseLM skill automation and the picker. Never infer or switch policy at runtime.

## User Stories

1. As a Codex or Claude user, I want native skills used without LouiseLM reinjecting them, so that skills are not duplicated.
2. As a custom-adapter user, I want to opt one agent into injected discovery, so that natural-language skill matching still works.
3. As a user, I want a picker that invokes a known local skill safely in both native and injected profiles, so that explicit activation is predictable.
4. As a user, I want skill context hidden before submission but inspectable afterward, so that chat stays clean without concealing what was sent.
5. As a skill author, I want malformed, shadowed, explicit-only, truncated, or inaccessible skills diagnosed clearly, so that configuration failures are understandable.
6. As a user configuring an unfamiliar ACP adapter, I want documentation explaining Agent Skills, ACP transport, host responsibilities, and filesystem assumptions, so that I can choose the correct policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Global `skills.policy` defaults to `native`; agent definitions may override only the policy, while paths remain global and session-static.
2. `native` sends no automatic catalog or skill body. Picker activation resolves against the adapter's latest advertised command list and sends exactly one advertised command plus task.
3. `inject` sends one hidden catalog only on the first accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, then sends a selected complete SKILL.md once per deliberate activation. It never falls back to native or reinjects after uncertain accepted requests.
4. `off` sends no skill automation and disables the skill picker without intercepting user-authored slash commands.
5. The old `full_content` setting and dormant automatic-native-fallback API are removed with clear migration errors and documentation.
6. Agent Skills core metadata is parsed with `lyaml` and semantically validated; Codex and Claude invocation-control extensions are recognized without treating them as ACP requirements.
7. Missing `lyaml` blocks injected sessions and local native picker/validation, but does not block native sessions themselves or off sessions.
8. The injected catalog uses the agreed Agent Skills XML shape, fixed behavioral preamble, XML escaping, and an 8,000-byte UTF-8-safe total budget with deterministic diagnostics.
9. Submitted prompt contexts are represented as one closed Neovim fold containing exact sent content in order; automatic hidden catalog text never appears as a pre-send marker.
10. README, generated configuration help/annotations, checkhealth, and migration guidance explain policy selection, no-double-send behavior, dependency installation, trust/path rules, filesystem limits, and live-only fold persistence.
11. Automated tests cover configuration, discovery, YAML, invocation metadata, native command correlation, injection lifecycle, slash deferral, failures/cancellation, no-double-send invariants, and context folds. Installed Codex/Claude checks remain documented manual smoke tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Agent Skills defines the skill format; ACP transports prompts and command updates; LouiseLM is the host responsible for policy and injected discovery.
- Explicit-only wins when `disable-model-invocation: true` or OpenAI's `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` is present. Such skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs.
- Root order defines duplicate precedence; path handling is deterministic, symlink-aware, and diagnostic without adding a trust database.
- The 8,000-byte mechanism intentionally mimics Codex's conservative fallback behavior; it is not part of ACP or the Agent Skills specification.
- Use native Neovim folds and existing context transport. Do not introduce a generic fold framework.

## Testing Notes

Use MiniTest for module behavior and a mock ACP agent for command updates and prompt transport. Test public behavior and exact no-double-send invariants. Do not require authenticated live adapters in automated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Runtime policy switching or inference.
- A general UI for every ACP advertised command.
- A LouiseLM ACP filesystem service.
- Recursive embedding of skill resources.
- Persistent transcript reconstruction.
- Automatic dependency installation.
- Generic adapter-native skill implementation.
- Tool-call fold rendering; track that as a separate design question.

title: Diagnose installed lyaml outside Neovim search paths
description:
## Problem

Local skill discovery reports:

```
louiselm: lyaml is required for local skill discovery; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml`
```

However, LuaRocks confirms that lyaml is already installed for Lua 5.1. The actual failure is that the active Neovim process does not search the LuaRocks tree, so the message sends the user toward an installation command that will not fix the search-path mismatch.

## Reproduction evidence

- `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 show lyaml` succeeds with lyaml 6.2.9-2 under `$HOME/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/luarocks`.
- Neovim 0.12.2 embeds LuaJIT 2.1.
- In `nvim --headless -u NONE`, `pcall(require, "lyaml")` returns `module 'lyaml' not found`.
- Neovim's `package.path` and `package.cpath` contain system paths, but not the asdf LuaRocks share/lib paths reported by `luarocks path --lua-version 5.1`.

## Expected behavior

When lyaml cannot be loaded, LouiseLM should preserve enough of the loader failure to distinguish an absent installation from an installed-but-unreachable LuaRocks tree (and from native module load failures), then give a corrective action that matches the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user-facing/checkhealth diagnostic distinguishes at least package-not-found/search-path mismatch from a native loader failure instead of always saying to install lyaml.
2. Documentation gives a supported way to make a Lua 5.1 LuaRocks tree visible to Neovim, including non-system/asdf installs.
3. Tests cover the generic `require("lyaml")` failure mapping without depending on a real LuaRocks installation.
4. Diagnostics do not expose unrelated environment values or sensitive data.
close_reason: Shortened interactive lyaml failures to point at checkhealth, added detailed persistent zsh/asdf guidance to health and README, and covered both surfaces. Verified 181 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.
