title: Open every UI selector outside insert mode
description:
## Problem

Commit 1eb309a fixed permission selection by leaving insert mode immediately before vim.ui.select. That diagnosis is correct: Chat:attach enters insert mode, and list-focused select providers can otherwise receive the wrong mode and confirm or edit the wrong picker state.

The same bug remains in session configuration. Chat:attach schedules open_session_options after entering insert mode, while both the options overview and its nested model/value picker call vim.ui.select without normalizing mode. This affects the automatic first-session overview and can also affect :LouiselmSessionOptions when invoked from an insert-mode mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a ready session that advertises a model or boolean configuration option.
2. Let Chat:attach focus the prompt and enter insert mode.
3. Wait for the scheduled initial options overview, or invoke :LouiselmSessionOptions from an insert-mode mapping.
4. Observe that vim.ui.select is called while the inherited mode is insert; with a list-focused provider, navigation or confirmation targets the wrong picker state.
5. Select an option such as Model and observe the nested value picker has the same unnormalized boundary.

## Investigation

There are 12 vim.ui.select call sites across chat, context, and diff UI. In addition to session options, selectors that are asynchronous, nested, or exposed through public Chat methods can inherit insert mode: resumed-session selection, remembered-permission selection and confirmation, session switch/close, agent selection, and file/skill context selection. The permission picker is now protected. The diff-review selector is currently protected indirectly because the focused diff buffer exits insert mode before its normal-mode actions run.

## Scope

- Normalize mode at the narrowest shared LouiseLM selection boundary immediately before opening every vim.ui.select picker.
- Cover both stages of the session-options flow, especially the model/value picker opened by :LouiselmSessionOptions and the automatic picker scheduled by Chat:attach.
- Migrate or audit every raw vim.ui.select call in lua/louiselm/ui so no insert-mode-sensitive sibling remains.
- Preserve provider ownership of picker layout and interaction; do not detect or configure Snacks or another provider.
- Preserve selection values, cancellation behavior, asynchronous scheduling, and disposal guards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The automatically opened session-options overview is invoked outside insert mode after Chat:attach starts the prompt in insert mode.
2. The nested model/boolean value picker is also invoked outside insert mode.
3. Every LouiseLM vim.ui.select call either uses the shared normalization boundary or has a tested invariant proving insert mode cannot reach it.
4. The existing permission-picker mode regression remains green, and diff review remains in normal mode.
5. Headless behavioral tests cover the session-options regression and at least one representative shared/public or asynchronous selector path without relying on provider internals.
6. The focused UI tests, full MiniTest suite, StyLua check, and lua-language-server check pass.
close_reason: Normalized all 12 vim.ui.select call sites through one normal-mode picker boundary. Added red-green regressions for automatic/nested session options and file context selection. Verification: focused chat 44/44, context 5/5, diff 5/5; full MiniTest 185/185; StyLua and LuaLS passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Keep the chat header compact instead of dumping session metadata
description:
## Problem

The chat buffer header expands into a long Markdown heading containing every session option and context field. At normal split widths it wraps across visual rows, dominates the top of the conversation, and is difficult to scan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session whose agent reports several configuration options plus context or cost telemetry.
2. Display the chat in a typical narrow vertical split.
3. Observe that the level-one Markdown heading includes all metadata and wraps across multiple visual rows.

## Observed

A Codex session currently renders a heading such as:

`# codex · session-1 · ready · Mode=agent-full-access · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off · context=62585/258400 (24% normal) · Your turn`

title: Recover and resume ACP sessions
description:
## Problem Statement

Recovering an existing ACP conversation currently requires users to know the adapter name, exact ACP session ID, adapter configuration, and working directory, then execute Lua manually. Normal users need a discoverable resume flow without losing the current chat.

## Solution

Add a `:LouiseLmResume` flow that discovers recoverable sessions from configured ACP adapters, filters them to the current workspace by default, and loads the selected session into a separate chat buffer. Keep the public Lua load API as the underlying and advanced recovery path.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to pick a prior session from a list so I can continue work without remembering opaque ACP IDs.
2. As a user, I want the default list limited to the current workspace so unrelated sessions do not overwhelm me.
3. As a user, I want an explicit all-workspaces view so older sessions remain recoverable.
4. As a user, I want resuming to preserve my current chat and open the recovered conversation separately.
5. As a user, I want load failures explained without silently creating a new session.
6. As an advanced user, I want the Lua `load_session` API to remain available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given configured adapters that support session listing, the resume flow lists sessions with available adapter, workspace, display name, and activity metadata.
2. Given the default resume view, only sessions for the current workspace are shown; an explicit action reveals other workspaces.
3. Given a selected session, louiselm uses the current configured adapter definition and ACP `session/load`, then attaches it to a new chat buffer.
4. Given an existing attached chat, resuming does not replace or dispose it.
5. Given a missing, unsupported, or failed session load, the UI reports the specific failure and does not create a replacement session.
6. Given a loaded session, ACP-replayed history appears in the new chat before it is marked ready.
7. Given a session adapter cannot list sessions, exact-ID loading remains available through the public Lua API.
8. A lightweight local cache may accelerate discovery, but the ACP adapter remains authoritative; stale entries are handled as load failures and can be removed.
9. Session identity is scoped by adapter, ACP session ID, and workspace; old adapter commands are never reused.

## Implementation Notes

- Build on the existing session registry/API and chat attach lifecycle.
- Add ACP session-list support only where advertised; preserve graceful fallback for adapters without it.
- Keep discovery/cache state separate from conversation history.
- Use the existing asynchronous callback/event model and test production scheduling boundaries.

## Testing Notes

- Test listing/filtering and stable session identity across adapters and workspaces.
- Test successful load/replay/attach without disturbing an existing chat.
- Test unsupported listing, missing sessions, adapter failures, and no silent new-session fallback.
- Test the public Lua load path remains functional.

## Out of Scope

- Changing ACP persistence semantics or adapter storage.
- Reusing historical adapter commands.
- Automatically deleting adapter-side sessions.
- Reconstructing conversation history from louiselm cache data.

description:
## Reproduction

title: Render persistent telemetry and grouped session diagnostics
description:
## Goal

Keep live, actionable session telemetry visible throughout long conversations while preserving a complete, copyable diagnostic block at the top of the chat transcript. Preserve adapter-provided values quasi as-is and make ACP versus LouiseLM-derived information visually distinguishable for QA.

## Reference

The motivating session rendered one long wrapped heading containing the ACP report id, local session id, lifecycle state, skills state, five adapter options, context usage, and turn label. Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260816_0632_948x1084_1786854748.png.

This task supersedes the design scope left after louiselm-kuc, whose persistent turn label was already implemented by commit 106aa9c. It builds on the completed compact-header work in louiselm-dv9 without reopening that historical task.

## Persistent Winbar Contract

Use the existing window-local winbar as the single persistent surface. Render fields in this order when available:

    Your turn · context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the existing friendly lifecycle labels: Your turn, Model responding, Waiting for permission, Stopping, Starting, Error, and Unavailable.
- Give lifecycle states semantic ready/active/warning/error styling; semantic urgency takes precedence over provenance styling.
- Render adapter-reported context used/size quasi as-is with ACP provenance styling.
- Render only the LouiseLM-derived percentage in parentheses with derived provenance styling. Do not display the normal/elevated/high/critical pressure taxonomy.
- After a model change, retain the last context reading and append an explicit derived stale marker until a fresh adapter usage update arrives.
- Render cumulative cost quasi as-is only after the adapter reports it. Retain the last reported cumulative cost when later usage updates omit cost; remove it when the adapter explicitly clears it. Never invent zero, unknown, or unsupported placeholders.
- If context or cost has never been reported, omit that segment.
- Do not include session identity, model, mode, adapter options, or tool activity in the winbar. Tool activity remains in chronological transcript messages.
- Keep all telemetry on this one surface. Do not add a statusline, tabline, floating HUD, or pinned split.

## Transcript Diagnostic Contract

Replace the single unbounded heading with one contiguous, complete block using one compact logical line per category:

    # codex/ACP_SESSION_ID · session-1
    Session: status=ready · display=Your turn · skills=native
    ACP options: Mode=agent · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off
    Telemetry: context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the full ACP report identity and local session identity in the first line.
- Preserve both raw LouiseLM lifecycle status and its friendly display label so copied QA evidence exposes their mapping.
- Show the exact skills policy: native, inject, or off. Do not collapse native and inject into on.
- Preserve adapter option names, typed current values, and adapter order on one compact logical line. Allow normal Neovim wrapping; do not add width-dependent packing or one-option-per-line rendering.
- Deliberately duplicate context and cost in the diagnostic block and winbar. The winbar is the live HUD; the transcript block is the complete copyable snapshot. Both must render from the same session state and formatting logic so they cannot disagree.
- Keep the block current when lifecycle state, configuration options, context, cost, or stale state changes.

## Provenance and Rendering

- Use explicit section labels as the primary provenance signal: Session for LouiseLM state and ACP options for adapter configuration. These labels survive copying.
- In mixed telemetry, use named user-overridable highlight groups for ACP values and LouiseLM-derived values. Do not hard-code colors.
- Keep textual structure sufficient without color: raw counts remain separate from parenthesized percentage/stale annotations.
- Escape statusline syntax in all dynamic winbar segments before composing highlight directives. Adapter-originated text must not be able to alter winbar formatting.
- Do not let provenance coloring weaken semantic error or permission states.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Scrolling a long chat keeps the friendly lifecycle label, exact reported context counts, derived percentage, stale validity, and optional last-reported cost visible in the window-local winbar.
2. Adapters that omit context or cost produce no fabricated values or placeholders, and explicit cost clearing removes the persistent cost.
3. Context pressure words are absent from both persistent and diagnostic displays; the derived percentage remains.
4. The transcript starts with the four logical diagnostic categories above, remains contiguous and copyable, uses exact skills policy and ACP option order, and intentionally duplicates live telemetry.
5. Raw status and friendly display label update together for every lifecycle state. Header and winbar telemetry cannot diverge because they share canonical formatting.
6. Provenance remains understandable without color and is additionally visible through user-overridable highlight groups; dynamic winbar content is statusline-escaped.
7. Existing winbar save/restore, session switching, disposal, scheduling, and late-event safety remain intact.
8. Headless tests cover lifecycle changes, context and cost updates/omission/clearing, model-change staleness, exact skills policies, several ACP options, provenance highlights, statusline escaping, and restoration. Include a manual narrow-split smoke check rather than width-specific pixel assertions.
9. README documents the persistent telemetry, grouped diagnostic block, provenance meaning, optional adapter fields, and last-reported cost semantics.

## Out of Scope

- A session-info copy command; add it only after real QA copying friction.
- Persistent session identity, model, mode, configuration, or tool activity.
- LouiseLM context pressure classifications.
- Width-aware option packing, per-option vertical rows, a generic statusline framework, or additional sticky UI surfaces.

title: Separate the first assistant output from the user blockquote
description:
## Problem
The first assistant output after a submitted prompt is not visually separated from the user turn and can inherit the pink Markdown blockquote styling. This makes the first commentary and following tool-call line look like part of the user message.

## Reproduction
1. Open a LouiseLM chat buffer and submit a prompt.
2. Have the agent emit a text chunk as its first event, followed by a tool call.
3. Observe the boundary between the final line of the `> ` user prompt and the initial assistant commentary/tool timeline.

## Observed
- The initial assistant commentary begins immediately below the user prompt with no blank separator.
- The first tool-call line follows inside the same visually pink region.
- In `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png`, lines 4 onward initially appear attached to the user turn and inherit its pink presentation.

## Expected
Every assistant turn begins as a visually distinct transcript block. Assistant commentary and tool-call lines must not inherit the user prompt blockquote styling, regardless of which event arrives first.

## Likely Root Cause
`Chat:submit()` creates a single empty response placeholder immediately after the `> ` prompt. The first `chunk` event replaces that placeholder with response text instead of preserving a blank turn separator. With the chat buffer using Markdown filetype, text directly following a blockquote can be parsed as a lazy continuation, so the initial assistant content and adjacent tool-call lines inherit the blockquote highlight. This is a rendering-boundary issue; do not special-case tool colors unless investigation disproves it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A blank separator remains between each submitted user blockquote and the first assistant transcript content.
2. Initial assistant text and tool-call lines render outside the user blockquote/pink region.
3. The boundary is correct when the first event is a text chunk, tool call, error, or other transcript-producing event.
4. Streaming multiple chunks and updating a started tool call in place do not accumulate extra blank lines or disturb chronological order.
5. Existing prompt placement, cursor behavior, and subsequent-turn rendering remain unchanged.
6. Add a headless behavioral regression test that asserts the buffer lines for a submitted prompt followed by asynchronously scheduled chunk and tool events; exercise the real scheduling boundary rather than only invoking the renderer synchronously.

## Notes
Fix the shared transcript/turn boundary rather than applying presentation logic to one tool-call event. Buffer-line behavior is the primary assertion; no pixel test is required.

title: LouiseLM attention control plane: ideas into reality
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arrive faster than sustained human attention can evaluate and realize them. Existing agent tools automate isolated conversations and coding turns but do not make the whole workflow, its authority boundaries, or its human-attention gates observable.

## Solution

Build LouiseLM as an attention control plane that turns ideas into reality. It makes workflow topology explicit, automates work agents can safely perform, and surfaces only decisions where human judgment materially improves or unblocks the outcome. LouiseLM ships an explicit software-delivery reference preset while allowing other workflows to configure different stages and resolvers.

The first active vertical slice is durable speech capture from Android and Neovim into one local Linux inbox. Later idea modelling, triage, workflow history, attention visualization, sequential orchestration, and parallel workers remain dependency-shaped deferred features.

## Implementation Decisions

- Human attention is assigned per transition, never by one global human-or-agent rule.
- Declarative validated topology describes stages, transitions, triggers, and resolvers; typed providers perform effects.
- Raw capture is immutable and local-first. Android and Neovim speech are the first bundled capture providers.
- Neovim is the cockpit; a narrow Rust user service owns durable capture ingestion and transcription while the editor is closed.
- The reference workflow is triage -> human/agent grill -> automatic plan and critique -> tracker DAG -> policy-controlled execution -> automated evidence -> human outcome acceptance.
- Logical workflow threads outlive replaceable ACP sessions and preserve decisions, supersessions, questions, evidence, and handoffs.
- The live idea journey and its expanding task DAG are the primary visualization. Human gates are visually distinct.
- Beads is the tracker in the reference preset, not a core dependency or a second implementation inside LouiseLM.
- Sequential execution precedes the committed parallel-worker milestone.

## Testing Decisions

Each executable boundary has deterministic tests. The capture milestone additionally requires a physical Android-to-Linux-to-Neovim dogfood test and explicit human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

The first slice does not implement semantic idea segmentation, triage actions, workflow orchestration, graph UI, or parallel workers. Those remain visible deferred children with evidence-based entry criteria.

title: Durable speech capture from Android and Neovim
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arising away from the keyboard are currently kept in memory or Gmail drafts and can be lost. Capture must be faster than classification and must not require Neovim to remain open.

## Solution

Record short speech streams from Android and Neovim, preserve the original audio in a local Linux inbox, transcribe asynchronously, and expose quiet durable status in Neovim. Android saves first and syncs later; no project, title, or priority is requested during capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Make skill discovery deterministic and symlink-aware
description:
## Goal

Discover local skills predictably across configured roots while preserving useful paths and diagnosing duplicates or unsafe-looking topology.

## Scope

- In scope: process global skill roots in configuration order; within each root sort deterministically by skill name and configured path.
- In scope: first valid duplicate skill name wins, later names are reported as shadowed, and the same canonical file is deduplicated.
- In scope: expand absolute paths and `~`; resolve relative roots against the session working directory. Health checks resolve them against Neovim's current working directory and say so.
- In scope: support symlinked roots and skill directories, detect canonical cycles/duplicates, preserve the configured-root alias in advertised absolute locations, and warn when a symlink resolves outside its root.
- In scope: continue past unreadable or invalid individual skills with one deduplicated user warning and full details available to diagnostics.
- In scope: refresh discovery whenever the picker opens and read the selected file at selection time.
- Out of scope: automatic project-local roots, a trust database, policy transport, and catalog budgeting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root order, not global absolute sorting, decides duplicate-name precedence.
2. Discovery order and diagnostics are stable across runs.
3. Canonical aliases do not create duplicate skills or traversal loops.
4. Catalog/picker locations preserve the user-configured alias rather than exposing a canonical dotfiles target.
5. Escapes outside a configured root remain usable but produce a source-to-target warning.
6. Relative-root behavior is covered for both sessions and checkhealth.
7. MiniTest covers duplicate names, identical canonical files, symlinked roots/directories, cycles, outside-root targets, unreadable files, and picker refresh behavior.

## Testing

Use temporary directory fixtures with real symlinks where supported. Keep path-policy tests separate from YAML semantic fixtures.

## Notes

Configured skill roots are trusted prompt/plugin-like input. Diagnostics inform the user; they do not create a new authorization system.

title: Refuse louiselm command pickers while a permission decision is open
description:
After 0ed18d0 (louiselm-brx) the chat presents one permission decision at a time, but that queue only covers agent-initiated permission requests. The pickers louiselm opens for its own commands - file, skill, session resume, session switch, agent choice, remembered-permission management, session options - are still unqueued. Opening one while a permission picker is up makes an async provider such as the Snacks picker tear the permission picker down, its on_close fires with no item, and the request is answered cancelled without the user deciding.

Severity after 0ed18d0 is a lost prompt and a spuriously denied tool call, not a hang: the cancelled response releases the decision slot and the queue advances. That is why this is a task rather than a P0/P1 bug.

## Decision: refuse these pickers, do not queue them

Queuing every Picker.select behind the decision slot was considered and rejected:

1. Chained pickers would deadlock. Several flows open a picker from inside another picker callback: manage_permissions (rules -> revoke confirm), open_session_options (option -> value), and critically lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua:114, where a review with several allow lifetimes opens a second picker WHILE holding the decision slot. That slot is only released when the second picker answers, so queuing it makes each wait on the other - the exact failure class louiselm-4wx and louiselm-brx removed.
2. Delayed popups steal input. A queued user-initiated picker opens at an arbitrary later moment, likely after the user moved on and started typing in the chat prompt, and the provider grabs input on open.
3. A leaked slot would freeze the whole UI instead of permissions only. Today a stuck decision still leaves the session picker and close_session reachable; behind one shared slot the escape hatches would be blocked too.
4. open_session_options auto-opens on state_changed -> ready and on attach (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1070 and :1370), so with two sessions a config picker would surface long after the state change that caused it.

Refusing has none of those properties, is smaller, and cannot deadlock.

## Scope

- While a permission decision is presented (chat decision_active), user-initiated picker commands return false plus an actionable message, e.g. "answer the open louiselm permission request first".
- The auto-opened session options picker is skipped rather than reported.
- Exceptions that stay allowed on purpose: close_session, because it is the escape hatch when a decision is stuck and cancelling that permission is the right outcome when the session is being closed anyway; and cancel, which is not a picker.
- The diff review lifetime picker is untouched: it belongs to the open decision rather than competing with it.

## Acceptance

- Each guarded command returns its refusal without opening a picker while a decision is open, and works normally once the decision is answered.
- close_session still opens its confirmation while a decision is open.
- A diff review with several allow lifetimes still opens its lifetime picker.
close_reason: Implemented in b76a95d as specified: refuse, not queue. DECISION_OPEN_ERROR guards Chat:manage_permissions, switch_session, session_options, pick_file, pick_skill, resume_session, and the agent-choice path of new_session; open_session_options also returns early so the automatic picker is skipped rather than reported. close_session and cancel stay unguarded on purpose, and the diff review lifetime picker is untouched. Test: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'refuses command pickers while a permission decision is open' covers every guarded command, proves no extra picker opens, proves close_session still opens its confirmation, and proves the commands work again once the decision is answered. Full suite 197 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. README documents the refusal and why it is not a queue.

title: Accept ACP nulls in session discovery
description:
## Problem

`:LouiselmResume` rejects valid ACP `session/list` responses when nullable fields are encoded as JSON `null`. Neovim decodes JSON `null` as `vim.NIL`, while discovery validation currently accepts only Lua `nil` or strings. A Codex response with `nextCursor: null` therefore reports `ACP session/list returned malformed data: nextCursor must be a string` and discards Codex sessions. The same mismatch affects nullable `SessionInfo.title` and `updatedAt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `nextCursor: null` is treated as end-of-pagination.
2. `title: null` and `updatedAt: null` are accepted and exposed as absent optional values.
3. Non-null, non-string values for all three fields remain rejected.
4. A regression test exercises the JSON-null representation through session discovery.
5. Focused tests, full mini.test, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Explain the LouiseLM vision and recursive identity
description:
## Problem Statement

The README documents development and implemented APIs but does not explain why LouiseLM exists, what the name means, or how its current ACP-backed Neovim foundation relates to the larger idea-to-software vision. Readers cannot yet understand the project before reaching the technical reference.

## Solution

Add a clear product narrative and an original hero banner at the start of the README. Present LouiseLM as alpha software whose north star is turning ideas into software, explain the attention-preserving workflow and its safety boundaries, and show the current manual workflow as one replaceable configuration. Preserve the existing technical reference beneath a concise bridge describing what works today.

## User Stories

1. As a new reader, I want to understand LouiseLM and its recursive name immediately, so that I can decide whether the project matters to me.
2. As a potential user, I want the vision separated clearly from current alpha capabilities, so that I am inspired without being misled.
3. As a creative developer, I want to see a strong default workflow presented as configurable, so that I can imagine building a different workflow with the same substrate.
4. As an operator, I want the vision to preserve my attention, ownership, and approval authority, so that automation remains empowering and legible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README uses LouiseLM as the project name and includes the exact recursive acronym: LouiseLM Organizes Unruled Intelligent Systems into Emancipated Language Meshes.
2. The opening states that LouiseLM turns ideas into software and clearly labels the project as alpha software.
3. The motivation explains that ideas arrive faster than sustained attention and uses the gardening example without clinical or medical positioning.
4. The vision covers interruption-free capture, later enrichment and explainable triage, focused deliberation, planning, dependency-shaped execution, agent implementation and review, human approval, and an observable operator control plane.
5. Neovim is presented as the deliberate home and cockpit, with headless automation and optional future capture surfaces rather than a promised editor-independent runtime.
6. Local-first ownership, configurable workflow boundaries, strong defaults, replaceable parts, and policy-controlled automation are explicit principles.
7. The current grill-me to plan to beads to coding-agent flow appears as one possible configuration; grill-me, beads, bv, bvr, particular models, and CodeCompanion are not presented as LouiseLM requirements. CodeCompanion is not mentioned.
8. Current ACP chat and session capabilities are distinguished from unimplemented idea capture, ranking, orchestration, and dashboard work.
9. An original banner depicts Louise Michel within a decentralized mesh of people, agents, models, skills, tools, voice capture, ideas, and code. It uses a red, black, and white Commune-era printmaking aesthetic fused with a modern systems diagram, informed by Metelkova street-art energy, with no labels or explanatory text.
10. Existing technical instructions remain accurate and mostly intact beneath the new narrative.

## Implementation Notes

- Expand the top of the existing README rather than replacing the technical reference.
- Add one project-local raster hero asset and reference it with a repository-relative path.
- Use project voice: one brief empowering manifesto-like passage followed by concrete language.
- The visual carries the Louise Michel reference; do not explain that reference in prose.
- Emancipation concerns ideas, workflows, and user choice, never unbounded agent authority.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation and image generation do not require an artificial red test.
- Inspect the final Markdown structure and rendered image reference.
- Run formatting, static-analysis, test, and diff checks required by the repository contract; report any unavailable gate.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing idea storage, capture devices, voice transcription, scheduling, triage, orchestration, dashboards, or agent review.

title: Parse and validate Agent Skills metadata with lyaml
description:
## Goal

Replace LouiseLM's limited handwritten frontmatter parser with standards-compliant YAML parsing and a thin Agent Skills semantic validator.

## Scope

- In scope: load `lyaml` lazily whenever LouiseLM-managed local skill discovery is required; report a structured missing-dependency error and never install dependencies automatically.
- In scope: parse SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, validate required Agent Skills fields and known standard field types, and preserve the complete original SKILL.md for activation.
- In scope: recognize `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation`; explicit-only wins on conflict and emits a warning.
- In scope: when optional invocation metadata is malformed or unreadable, retain a core-valid skill as picker-visible, mark it explicit-only, and warn.
- In scope: validate `allowed-tools` as metadata without granting or bypassing ACP permissions; warn when a SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines.
- In scope: ignore unknown extension fields without rejecting or warning, and remove the handwritten YAML subset parser.
- Out of scope: root precedence, symlink traversal, policy selection, catalog transport, and automatic dependency installation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. YAML features supported by LibYAML parse without adding LouiseLM-specific syntax.
2. Invalid YAML or invalid required Agent Skills metadata omits only that skill and yields an actionable diagnostic.
3. Core-valid skills survive broken optional invocation metadata as explicit-only picker entries.
4. Both known invocation controls are honored, conflicts warn, and explicit-only wins.
5. Missing `lyaml` is distinguishable from malformed skill metadata.
6. `allowed-tools` cannot change LouiseLM permission decisions.
7. MiniTest covers valid metadata, YAML syntax errors, semantic errors, extension metadata, conflicts, unknown fields, allowed-tools, and the line-count warning.

## Testing

Use fixture SKILL.md files and assert the public parser/validator result plus diagnostics. Do not test the handwritten parser after removal.

## Notes

`lyaml` is an intentional LibYAML dependency because LouiseLM should not own a partial YAML parser.
close_reason: Replaced handwritten frontmatter parsing with lazy lyaml loading and Agent Skills semantic validation; added explicit-only metadata diagnostics, dependency failure handling, documentation, and passing focused/full gates
